newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN, PIPPEN IN BROTHER ACT AS BULLS BEAT KNICKS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN, PIPPEN IN BROTHER ACT AS BULLS BEAT KNICKS.

text.p: It was little brother early and big brother late as the Chicago Bulls taught the New York Knicks a lesson Thursday.

Scottie Pippen -- with a point to prove to Knicks forward Larry Johnson -- scored 18 of his 33 points in the first quarter and Michael Jordan got 20 of his 34 in the last 7 1/2 minutes to rally the defending champions to a 105-103 victory.

"He wanted to make a statement," Jordan said of Pippen. "He wanted to come in and play his game. I would do the same if I was in his shoes. It's like little brother, big brother. You step aside and let little brother fight his own fight. And when he got tired, big brother stepped in to help him out."
Johnson had been quoted as saying all Pippen did was pass the ball to Jordan, while Pippen had described Johnson as having done nothing in the NBA but collect money.
In addition to his early heroics, Pippen made a key -- and controversial -- late steal, calling timeout as he fell out of bounds with 26 seconds left.
Jordan, who was limited to 14 points over the first three quarters but was unstoppable down the stretch, finally missed a foul-line jumper after Pippen's save.
Luc Longley grabbed the offensive rebound and was fouled. He calmly sank both shots, snapping a 103-103 tie with 5.4 seconds left.
Chris Childs then missed a reverse layup and Charles Oakley could not handle the offensive rebound as the buzzer sounded.
"We let it get away and Michael got hot," Childs summed up for the Knicks, who had led by nine points with 9:09 to go.
The Bulls have won five straight and 13 of 14 as they march to a second straight 70-win season. Chicago could match its NBA record of 72 wins by winning its last four games.
Patrick Ewing scored 15 of his 20 points in the second half and Johnson added 19 for the Knicks, who are now just one-half game ahead of Atlanta for third place in the Eastern Conference.
In Miami, Tim Hardaway scored 30 points and Alonzo Mourning 26 as the Heat clinched the Atlantic Division title with their sixth straight win, 93-83 over the slumping Detroit Pistons.
The win was the 59th of the season for Miami and gave the Heat their first-ever division championship. Miami swept all four meetings with Detroit this season for the first time.

"It is a great night for us," Heat coach Pat Riley said. "We have a group of young, tenacious guys who don't quit. We know it is only a first step, but it gives us a good position from which to start."
The win left the Heat in position to avoid the Bulls until the Eastern Conference finals and set up a likely first-round matchup with intrastate rival Orlando.
In Dallas, Hersey Hawkins scored 17 points, Gary Payton added 15 and Terry Cummings had 14 as the Seattle Supersonics defeated the Mavericks 90-82.
The win moved Seattle one game ahead of the second-place Los Angeles Lakers in the Pacific Division.
But Seattle's All-Star forward Shawn Kemp continued his funk, missing all four of his shots from the field while committing five fouls and three turnovers in 31 minutes.
In Los Angeles, the Minnesota Timberwolves clinched their first-ever playoff berth with a 108-96 win over the Clippers.

Stephon Marbury scored 29 points in the third quarter for Minnesota, which had lost two straight games after a three-game winning streak moved them within one victory of clinching. Tom Gugliotta added 23 points and 15 rebounds.
In Sacramento, Kevin Johnson's knifing layup through the lane with 4.7 seconds left in regulation lifted the Phoenix Suns to their 11th straight victory, 101-99 over the Kings.
Wayman Tisdale led Phoenix with 19 points and John Williams added 15 for the Suns, who also posted their seventh consecutive road win.
Mitch Richmond scored 23 points to lead the Kings, who are three games behind the Clippers for the final Western Conference playoff spot.

At Golden State, Latrell Sprewell scored six of his 22 points in overtime and Joe Smith hit a pair of crucial free throws with 8.8 seconds to play as the Warriors handed the Denver Nuggets their sixth straight loss, 109-107.
Smith finished with 25 points and Chris Mullin 21 for the Warriors, who won for the fourth time in six games.
In Houston, Charles Barkley scored 21 points, grabbed 12 rebounds and handed out eight assists as the Rockets won their fourth straight, 102-94 over the Vancouver Grizzlies.
At New Jersey, Kendall Gill scored 23 points, including a three-pointer with 12.5 seconds left, as the Nets ended a five-game losing streak, 93-88 over the Milwaukee Bucks.
In San Antonio, Rasheed Wallace scored 19 points and Arvydas Sabonis 18 as the Portland Trail Blazers beat the Spurs 98-81, winning all four season meetings by at least 11 points.
In Toronto, Dennis Scott scored 20 points in three quarters and the Orlando Magic held the Raptors to their lowest point total ever, 105-69.
